{{Short description|Austrian mathematician}}
'''Gerhard Larcher''' is an Austrian mathematician and professor of [[financial mathematics]] at the [[Johannes Kepler University]] (JKU) in [[Linz]], [[Austria]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Gerhard Larcher |url=https://www.jku.at/institut-fuer-finanzmathematik-und-angewandte-zahlentheorie/ueber-uns/team/gerhard-larcher/ |website=JKU - Johannes Kepler Universität Linz |language=de}}</ref> He is the head of the Institute of Financial Mathematics.

== Career ==
Gerhard Larcher studied mathematics at the [[University of Salzburg]] from 1978 to 1982 and received his doctorate with the highest distinction [[sub auspiciis Praesidentis]] under [[Harald Niederreiter]] in 1985; he completed his postdoc in mathematics four years later.

From 1983 to 2000, Larcher worked at the University of Salzburg as an assistant professor and lecturer and from 1996 as an associate professor of mathematics. During this time he headed the Institute of Mathematics for two years. Since 1999 he was speaker and leader of the [[Austrian Science Fund|FWF-Research Center]] (FSP) ''[[number theory|Number-Theoretic]] [[Algorithm]]s and their Applications''.

In 2000, Larcher was appointed as a full [[professor]] of financial mathematics at the Johannes Kepler University (JKU) in Linz, Austria. Three years later, he founded the [[Investment management|asset management]] company Art In Finance in [[Vienna]], which developed and implemented [[alternative investment]] strategies. After years of strong profits, the [[Option (finance)|option]] strategies of Art In Finance sustained massive losses during the [[2008 financial crisis]].<ref name="crisis">{{cite news |title=Art in Finance: Massive Verluste infolge der Finanzkrise |url=https://www.fondsprofessionell.at/news/produkte/headline/art-in-finance-massive-verluste-infolge-der-finanzkrise-86972/ |access-date=29 June 2022 |work=www.fondsprofessionell.at |language=de}}</ref> The strategies were then adapted accordingly and successfully reintroduced. At the start of 2017, he withdrew from the company and the asset management business. From 2003 to 2005, he was the department head of financial mathematics at the Johann Radon Institute for Computational and Applied Mathematics at the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="ricam">{{cite web |title=RICAM - Former Members |url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/ricam/people/formermembers |website=Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften}}</ref>

Since 2014 he has been the speaker of the Austrian special research area ''Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods: Theory and Applications''<ref name="qmc">{{cite web |title=Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods: Theory and Applications |url=http://www.sfb-qmc.jku.at/ |website=Johannes Kepler Universität Linz}}</ref> at the [[Austrian Science Fund]].<ref name="fwf">{{cite web |title=FWF: QMC-Project |url=https://pf.fwf.ac.at/en/research-in-practice/project-finder/128486 |website=Austrian Science Fund}}</ref> In addition to his work at the Johannes Kepler University, Larcher runs seminars and workshops in the field of quantitative finance.

He is the author of the monograph ''Quantitative Finance: Strategien, Investments, Analysen''<ref name="quantitative-finance">{{cite book |last1=Larcher |first1=Gerhard |title=Quantitative Finance: Strategien, Investments, Analysen |date=2020 |publisher=Springer Gabler Wiesbaden |doi=10.1007/978-3-658-29158-7 |isbn=978-3-658-29158-7 |s2cid=226725186 |edition=1 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-658-29158-7 |access-date=29 June 2022 |language=de}}</ref> published by [[Springer Verlag|Springer-Gabler Verlag]], of the trilogy ''The Art of Quantitative Finance. Strategies, Investmens, Research'' by Springer and ''Die [[Black–Scholes model|Black-Scholes-Theorie]], In 100 Schritten vom Münzwurf zum Wirtschaftsnobelpreis''<ref name="black-scholes">{{cite book |last1=Larcher |first1=Gerhard |title=Die Black-Scholes-Theorie: In 100 Schritten vom Münzwurf zum Wirtschaftsnobelpreis |date=26 June 2022 |publisher=Springer Fachmedien Wiesbaden |isbn=978-3-658-37375-7 |edition=1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kqPxzgEACAAJ |access-date=29 June 2022 |language=de}}</ref> also published by Springer.

In 2019, he founded the ''Linz School of Quantitative Finance (LSQF)'', a work group at the JKU Linz that deals with finance consulting and the creation of highly specialized finance [[software]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Team |url=https://www.lsqf.org/team/ |publisher=Linz School of Quantitative Finance}}</ref> Among other things, the LSQF team developed the Fynup Ratio,<ref name="fynup-ratio">{{cite web |title=Bessere Fonds-Auswahl mit fynup-ratio |url=https://www.fynup.at/a/fynup-ratio |website=Fynup.at|language=de |date=10 June 2020}}</ref> a new method for measuring the quality of [[investment fund]]s based on [[machine learning]] techniques.

His work and research focuses on the development and analysis of trading strategies, the [[Valuation (finance)|valuation]] of [[Derivative (finance)|derivative finance products]], [[Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo]] and [[Quasi-Monte Carlo method|quasi-Monte Carlo]] methods and number theory.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Del Chicca |first1=Lucia |title=Hybrid Monte Carlo-Methods in Credit Risk Management |date=8 May 2014|class=math.NA |eprint=1405.1831 }}</ref>

== Awards ==
* Science Award of [[Rotary International|Rotary]] Austria (1987)
* Christian Doppler Prize for Natural Sciences (1988)
* The [[Kardinal Innitzer Prize]] for the Advancement of Natural Sciences (1994)<ref name="innitzer">{{cite web |title=Kardinal Innitzer Studienfonds - Preisträger |url=http://www.kardinal-innitzer-fonds.at/preistraeger.html |website=Kardinal Innitzer Studienfonds|language=de}}</ref>
* [[Prize of the Austrian Mathematical Society]] (1996)<ref name="oemg">{{cite web |title=OeMG Preise |url=https://www.oemg.ac.at/Preise.html |website=OeMG|language=de}}</ref>
* Edmund and Rosa Hlawa Prize for Mathematics of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] (1997)<ref name="hlawka">{{cite web |title=Preisträger/innen des Edmund und Rosa Hlawka-Preises für Mathematik |url=https://stipendien.oeaw.ac.at/preise/naturwissenschaften/edmund-und-rosa-hlawka-preis-fuer-mathematik/preistraeger-innen |website=OEAW|language=de}}</ref>
